thread:
noor: Heads up — onboarding hit a snag. I followed the Linux quickstart on WSL2 but `redwoodctl login` fails to complete. Using tarball install, created profile 'project-x' but `redwoodctl serve --local` says "no active profile".

ben: Did init actually write profiles file? Check `cat ~/.config/redwoodctl/profiles.json` and `stat ~/.config/redwoodctl`.

noor: `stat` shows root:root on ~/.config/redwoodctl, must have run the binary with sudo by accident. I fixed ownership with chown and now `redwoodctl list-profiles` shows project-x.

lee: Cool — what about the login itself? Any error text?

noor: Device-code flow spins up and then after ~20s I get `polling failed: context deadline exceeded`. Browser reached the page and I approved, but CLI timed out before poll saw it.

ben: Which version? Old clients had a short poll window. `redwoodctl version`

noor: 0.11.9 (oops).

lee: Upgrade to 0.12.4 — fixed longer poll/retries and added `--timeout` flag. Also note quickstart scripts assume a profile called 'default' so if you name it something else you may need to set `REDWOODCTL_PROFILE=project-x` or run `redwoodctl init --default`.

noor: Upgraded and used `redwoodctl login --profile project-x --timeout 90s` and it worked. Filing a small quickstart patch suggestion: detect last-used profile or accept env var.

devex-bot: Created ticket #1620: "quickstart: respect existing profile name or honor REDWOODCTL_PROFILE" assigned to @lee

ben: Thanks for the repro — we'll add a WSL note about not running the binary with sudo and document the timeout flag.

noor: Appreciate it!
